name: Awwwards
role: primary, juried; award pages carry a jury score (0-10), award type and tags
robots_notes: User-agent * disallows /websites/? (query strings on the root listing only), /tag/, /gallery/, /search-websites, /preview/, /vote/ and a few profile paths. Collection listings with ?page=N and /sites/<slug> award pages are allowed. Checked 2026-10-24.
notes: Listings are plain HTML (~600 KB, ~31 cards per page). Each card carries the slug, title, tags and the live-site link; the award page /sites/<slug> carries the score badge (box-score__note) and 'Site of the Day - <date>'. --no-score skips award pages.

name: CSS Design Awards
role: primary, juried; award pages carry UI / UX / Innovation scores (0-10)
notes: Listing cards (article.single-project) carry category (NOMINEE / WOTD / WOTM), a month-day date, the award page link, the live-site link and, for winners, the JPANEL score. Award pages /sites/<slug>/<id>/ add the three vote scores (score = their mean), the full date and tags.

name: Behance (home feed)
role: volume source, noisy; only projects that link a live external website are kept
robots_notes: robots.txt disallows anthropic-ai, ClaudeBot and Claude-Web entirely, and for all agents disallows search URLs such as /search/*?*field=* (so the Product Design category search is off limits). The home page and /gallery/<id>/<slug> project pages are allowed for User-agent *. Checked 2026-10-24.
notes: The page is JS-rendered and bot-protected: the home feed answers HTTP 403 to automation while still rendering project cards (a[href*="/gallery/"]) in Playwright with a Chrome UA. The crawler therefore uses the home feed only, never search or category URLs, and keeps a project only when its page links an external website (url = that site, source_url = the project). Yield is low and unstable, so the supported path for Behance finds is /tasteful:add <url> [behance-project-url], including the assisted mode where Claude in Chrome reads the project page open in the user's own browser.

name: Manual additions
robots_notes: Not crawled; the user supplies the URL and probe.mjs fetches only that site.
notes: Anything found elsewhere (including Behance) goes through /tasteful:add <url> [source-url], which probes the site, proposes a tagged entry and asks before writing.
